stops.title: PhoneNumber accepts formatted and local numbers

mechanical.firstSentence: The PhoneNumber scalar no longer requires strict `+<7-15 digits>` input: it now also accepts spaces, dashes, parentheses, a missing plus sign, and space-separated trailing digits (the "extension").

judged.why: First sentence states the scalar now accepts looser, unformatted inputs, and the mismatch flag names the specific E.164 discrepancy to check.

stops.title: One regex drives all three entry points

mechanical.firstSentence: Output serialization, variable parsing and inline-literal parsing all accept the looser set of strings and report a new error text.

judged.why: First sentence says all three entry points now accept the looser strings with new error text, and it points to the docs/codegen/schema mismatch worth checking.

stops.title: New phone pattern: much looser, possible ReDoS

mechanical.firstSentence: Any string of at least 3 digits now passes, with no maximum length.

judged.why: First sentence plainly states any 3+ digit string now passes with no max length, and the danger/mismatch flags name the ReDoS risk and extension ambiguity.

stops.title: Error message text replaced in all three paths

mechanical.firstSentence: Rejected values now produce a longer "Invalid phone number: …" message instead of "Value is not a valid phone number of the form +17895551234 (7-15 digits)".

judged.why: First sentence states the error message text changed, and it names the risk that clients/tests matching old text will break.

stops.title: Tests now lock in acceptance of local and formatted numbers

mechanical.firstSentence: The tests now require that numbers without a plus sign and with spaces, dashes or parentheses parse, and that letters, brackets, padded parentheses and `+12` are rejected.

judged.why: First sentence states what inputs now parse or get rejected per the tests, and it explicitly lists untested gaps (length limit, parentheses, extension, perf) worth checking.

stops.title: Make $url() drop the trailing index segment

mechanical.firstSentence: Calling the URL helper on an index route now returns the real path, for example `http://fake/` instead of `http://fake/index`.

judged.why: States the concrete output change (returns / instead of /index) but only gives motivation/consistency rationale, not a specific risk to check.

stops.title: Index stripped after params and query are applied

mechanical.firstSentence: URLs built by the URL helper now lose a trailing `/index`, but the strip runs after path params and the query string are already added.

judged.why: First sentence states URLs now lose trailing /index and notes the ordering issue; body explicitly names two risky cases (query string, param valued 'index').

stops.title: WebSocket URLs still keep index

mechanical.firstSentence: The WebSocket helper does not change, so `client.index.$ws()` still connects to `.../index`.

judged.why: First sentence states $ws still connects to .../index (unchanged behavior); body explicitly flags a judgment call about whether $ws should match the fix.

stops.title: Tests cover root index, nested routes, params, query

mechanical.firstSentence: The new tests check that `$url()` gives `http://fake/` for the root index and correct hrefs for a mounted sub-app, a path param and a query.

judged.why: First sentence narrates what the new tests check rather than stating a behavior change; body explicitly names untested risky cases (query, nested index, param valued 'index').

stops.title: Wildcard plus credentials now reflects the caller

mechanical.firstSentence: With a wildcard origin and credentials enabled, the CORS middleware now echoes back whatever Origin the request sent, instead of sending `*`.

judged.why: First sentence states the echo-instead-of-wildcard change plainly, and the stop states the security consequence as a fact worth scrutinizing.

stops.title: Origin value and Vary header both change

mechanical.firstSentence: Two behaviors change, and only when credentials is true and origin is `*`.

judged.why: First sentence only announces that 'two behaviors change' without saying what they are; later it flags the default-origin case as an affected caller.

stops.title: Any origin, including null, now gets credentials

mechanical.firstSentence: Any site, including a sandboxed iframe or file page that sends `Origin: null`, can now make credentialed requests and read the responses.

judged.why: First sentence plainly states that any site including null-origin callers can now get credentialed access, and explicit danger/mismatch flags name judgment points.

stops.title: Vary: Origin added on credentialed wildcard responses

mechanical.firstSentence: Preflight and normal responses now include `Vary: Origin` when credentials is on, even with a wildcard origin.

judged.why: First sentence plainly states the new Vary: Origin behavior, but the rest only describes implementation mechanics without flagging a judgment call.

stops.title: Tests lock in reflection, including for null

mechanical.firstSentence: The tests lock in reflection for simple and preflight requests, a different value per origin, no allowed-origin header when the request has no Origin, and reflection of `null`.

judged.why: First sentence lists what the tests cover rather than stating a behavior change in plain terms, but the stop names specific untested gaps worth checking.

stops.title: ETag no longer depends on how a stream is split

mechanical.firstSentence: The same response body now gets the same ETag however the stream happens to split it into pieces.

judged.why: First sentence states callers now get the same ETag regardless of stream splitting, but nothing is flagged for the reviewer to judge.

stops.title: One function changed, used by every ETag response

mechanical.firstSentence: Only the body hashing changes: the stream is now cut into fixed 256 KiB blocks before hashing, and the hash is still chained block to block.

judged.why: First sentence narrates the implementation (cutting into 256 KiB blocks, chaining) rather than stating a caller-visible outcome, and the stop only maps scope without naming a specific risk.

stops.title: Body is hashed in fixed 256 KiB blocks

mechanical.firstSentence: Each block now feeds the chained hash at exactly 256 KiB, and only the final block can be shorter.

judged.why: First sentence describes the block-hashing mechanism rather than the caller-visible ETag change (which comes later), but the stop explicitly flags the buffer-reuse safety assumption as worth checking.

stops.title: Test: three-piece stream matches one-piece stream

mechanical.firstSentence: The new test requires that 1,000,000 zero bytes sent as one piece and as three uneven pieces (1 + 32,768 + 967,231) get the same ETag.

judged.why: First sentence states the invariant under test (same ETag across different chunkings), and the stop explicitly names coverage gaps (all-zero payload, no multi-chunk leftover, no concrete hash check).

stops.title: Stop spurious TimeoutError after successful requests

mechanical.firstSentence: Requests that finish before the timeout should no longer show a TimeoutError in browser devtools.

judged.why: First sentence states the user-visible fix (no spurious TimeoutError) but the stop never flags a specific risk or judgment call.

stops.title: Timeout no longer races; aborts without guard

mechanical.firstSentence: When the timer runs out, the caller still gets a TimeoutError, but the fetch is now aborted right away instead of 1ms later.

judged.why: First sentence states the behavior change (immediate abort, still throws TimeoutError) and the stop explicitly flags the missing guard and resulting unhandled rejection as risks to check.

stops.title: Forward non-standard options like Next.js `next` to fetch

mechanical.firstSentence: Options Ky doesn't recognise, and that the Request object doesn't keep, now reach the fetch function as its second argument.

judged.why: First sentence plainly states unrecognised options now reach fetch as a second argument, but the stop gives no specific risk or case to check.

stops.title: Three pieces: key registry, filter, fetch call sites

mechanical.firstSentence: The only runtime change is that fetch now gets a second argument, both when timeouts are off and in the timeout wrapper.

judged.why: First sentence states fetch now gets a second argument on both paths, but the rest just maps files with no judgment call named.

stops.title: An option is unknown if it's not a Ky option and not on Request

mechanical.firstSentence: Any option key that isn't one of Ky's own names, and isn't a property of the built Request object, gets copied into the init object for fetch.

judged.why: First sentence states unknown-key options are copied into fetch's init, and it names duplex/priority/dispatcher/window plus the runtime-dependence to check.

stops.title: Fetch receives the init object on both paths

mechanical.firstSentence: Every request, including each retry, now calls fetch with the cloned Request plus the unknown-options object, whether or not a timeout is set.

judged.why: First sentence states every call now passes init to fetch including retries, and it flags custom-fetch wrappers treating init as an override to check.

stops.title: Ky's own option names now live in one list

mechanical.firstSentence: Ky's own options are now listed once, as a `KyOptions` type plus a matching runtime object.

judged.why: First sentence describes a type/code restructuring (KyOptions type and object) rather than a user-visible behavior change, but it does flag the interface-merging comment to check.

stops.title: Test locks in forwarding of a `next` option

mechanical.firstSentence: The new test checks that a `next` option arrives at a custom fetch, by reference, in the init object.

judged.why: First sentence states the observed behavior (next option arrives by reference in init), and the stop names untested paths and fields as gaps to check.

stops.title: Typo fix in the before-request hook docs

mechanical.firstSentence: Nothing changes at runtime.

judged.why: First sentence states runtime behavior is unchanged, but the stop never flags anything specific for reviewer judgment.

stops.title: Two misspellings corrected in a comment

mechanical.firstSentence: The before-request hook's description in editor hover text now reads "for example, modify `options.headers`".

judged.why: First sentence gives the corrected hover text and the stop explicitly checks/rules out other copies of the typo needing fixes.

stops.title: Watch only the env files Vite actually loads

mechanical.firstSentence: The dev server should stop watching the whole env directory and watch only the four env files for the current mode.

judged.why: First sentence states watcher now covers only four mode files instead of the whole dir, and the stop flags the missing test/weak assertion as a judgment point.

stops.title: One helper now returns full paths; three callers

mechanical.firstSentence: Three behaviors change: which paths the file watcher subscribes to, how the env loader finds files, and how a change is recognized as an env change that restarts the server.

judged.why: First sentence lists the three behavior changes (watch set, loader lookup, restart detection) but the rest only says callers 'have to cope' without naming a specific risk.

stops.title: Env file list now holds full paths under the env dir

mechanical.firstSentence: The helper that lists env files for a mode now returns full paths such as `<envDir>/.env.development`, not bare names.

judged.why: First sentence says the helper now returns full paths instead of bare names, and it explicitly flags checking separator consistency across callers.

stops.title: Editing .env may no longer restart the dev server

mechanical.firstSentence: Saving an env file appears to no longer count as an env change, so the dev server may not restart.

judged.why: First sentence says editing env files may no longer restart the server, and it names the exact basename-vs-absolute-path mismatch plus a danger flag.

stops.title: Watcher subscribes to four env files, not the env dir

mechanical.firstSentence: The dev server's file watcher now watches the root, the config dependencies, and the four mode-specific env file paths, instead of the whole env directory.

judged.why: First sentence states the watcher now subscribes to specific files instead of the directory, and it names risks like missed new files and dropped dedupe.
